simple_definition: The robot transport network in a chip factory that carries boxes of wafers between machines.
technical_definition: Overhead hoist transport vehicles, stockers, buffers, lifts and the material control software that move wafer carriers between tools, handing off at load ports per SEMI E84.
where_used: Front-end fabs; increasingly back-end packaging plants

simple_definition: Small vehicles that run on rails on the factory ceiling and lower wafer boxes onto machines.
technical_definition: Ceiling-suspended rail vehicles that carry FOUPs between tools, buffers and stockers across floors and buildings; the core of 300 mm AMHS.

simple_definition: The sealed plastic box that holds a batch of 300 mm wafers as they move around the factory.
technical_definition: Standard 300 mm wafer carrier (SEMI E47.1) transported by AMHS and docked at tool load ports; may be nitrogen-purged.

simple_definition: A tall automated shelf where wafer boxes wait between production steps.
technical_definition: Automated storage unit for carriers (FOUPs) within the AMHS, sometimes with nitrogen purge; under-track buffers are smaller variants.

simple_definition: The software that tells the transport robots which wafer box to move where.
technical_definition: Factory software that schedules and executes carrier moves by the AMHS on request from the MES or dispatcher.

simple_definition: The set of rules 300 mm chip factories require machines to follow so they can be run fully automatically.
technical_definition: SEMI E39/E40/E87/E90/E94/E116/E148/E157 on top of SECS-II, HSMS and GEM (E30), as listed in SEMI E192.
where_used: Equipment purchase specifications for 300 mm fabs

simple_definition: The network method (like the internet) machines use to send factory-standard messages to control computers.
technical_definition: SEMI E37 High-Speed SECS Message Services: TCP/IP transport for SECS-II messages, replacing serial SECS-I.

simple_definition: A factory computer's instructions to a machine: which recipe to run on which wafers (process job), grouped per wafer box (control job).
technical_definition: SEMI E40 process jobs specify the recipe and material; SEMI E94 control jobs group process jobs for one or more carriers; process jobs must exist before the control job that links them.

simple_definition: A second data connection on each factory machine that lets several analysis programs pull detailed sensor data at once.
technical_definition: SEMI EDA suite (E120, E125, E132, E134 etc.) using SOAP/XML web services; supplements SECS/GEM, supports multiple concurrent clients and self-describing metadata.
where_used: FDC, APC, predictive maintenance data collection

simple_definition: A request telling a machine which measurements and events to send, and how often.
technical_definition: SEMI E134 object listing trace, event and exception requests that an EDA client defines and activates on equipment.

simple_definition: Automatically tweaking a machine recipe after each batch based on how the last batch measured, so results stay on target.
technical_definition: A form of advanced process control in which metrology after a step feeds a model that adjusts recipe parameters for the next lot or wafer (feedback) or downstream steps (feedforward).

simple_definition: Watching measurements on charts and raising an alarm when they drift outside normal limits.
technical_definition: Control-chart monitoring of process and metrology parameters; violations stop processing and trigger an out-of-control action plan.

simple_definition: The checklist engineers follow to fix a machine or process after an alarm.
technical_definition: Defined troubleshooting and disposition steps triggered by an SPC or FDC violation, increasingly run in workflow software.

simple_definition: A central library that stores and controls the exact settings each machine uses.
technical_definition: Software that centralises, validates and version-controls equipment recipes across tools and fabs.

simple_definition: Software that picks which batch of wafers each machine should work on next.
technical_definition: Rule- or optimisation-based selection of the next lot for a tool, triggered by machine events, part of or linked to the MES.

simple_definition: The full set of factory software that runs a chip plant together.
technical_definition: Integrated fab software stack (MES, dispatching, equipment automation, MCS, SPC/FDC/APC, yield) connected to equipment via SEMI standards.

simple_definition: The software link that connects each machine to the factory system.
technical_definition: Middleware/cell controller that translates MES commands into SECS/GEM messages for equipment and collects equipment data.

simple_definition: A standard way to say whether a machine is producing, idle, being repaired, etc., so everyone measures uptime the same way.
technical_definition: Six mutually exclusive states (productive, standby, engineering, scheduled downtime, unscheduled downtime, non-scheduled) underlying MTBF, MTTR, availability and utilization metrics.

simple_definition: Throwing out chips that pass the test but behave oddly compared with the rest of their batch, because they are more likely to fail later.
technical_definition: AEC-Q001 statistical outlier screening using robust mean and sigma with static or per-lot/wafer dynamic limits.

simple_definition: A newer standard for chip test data that can be streamed live instead of waiting for files.
technical_definition: SEMI E183 Rich Interactive Test Database: relational container (superset of STDF content) plus MQTT publish-subscribe streaming with provenance metadata.

simple_definition: Frost & Sullivan's umbrella term in China for all factory-running software in chip and related plants.
technical_definition: Category covering MES, APS, RTD, EAP, MCS, test management, data collection, YMS, engineering data analysis and SPC for semiconductor, display, PCB and PV manufacturing.
